rationale: Per WHO 5th ed, central conventional chondrosarcoma is a chondrogenic BONE tumor that is intramedullary in origin, so it is restricted to the skeletal (C40/C41) codes and does not arise in the laryngeal (C32), nasal cavity (C300) or paranasal sinus (C31) sites also present in this code's ceiling.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma, summarizing WHO 5th ed

rationale: Grade 1 (conventional) chondrosarcoma NOS is a generic graded cartilaginous malignancy occurring across the code's ceiling, including bone as well as laryngeal and sinonasal cartilage; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma

rationale: Central (intramedullary) low-grade chondrosarcoma is by definition an intraosseous bone tumor, restricted to the skeletal codes and not the laryngeal/nasal/sinus soft-cartilage sites in the ceiling.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma, WHO 5th ed

rationale: Peripheral chondrosarcoma arises within the cartilage cap of a pre-existing osteochondroma (a bone-surface lesion), so it is a skeletal tumor restricted to bone (C40/C41), not the laryngeal/nasal/sinus sites in the ceiling.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma, WHO 5th ed

rationale: Secondary peripheral chondrosarcoma develops from the cartilage cap of an osteochondroma and is a chondrogenic bone tumor per WHO 5th ed; it is restricted to skeletal sites and does not arise in the larynx/nasal cavity/sinus present in the ceiling.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma, WHO 5th ed

rationale: Chondroblastoma occurs throughout the skeleton (long bones, flat bones, pelvis, spine, ribs, hands/feet and craniofacial bones), so within its bone-only ceiling it is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Archives of Pathology & Laboratory Medicine - Chondroblastoma: An Update

rationale: EMC arises in deep soft tissue across the body (proximal extremities/limb girdles most common, but also trunk, retroperitoneum, head and neck), spanning its soft-tissue-only ceiling; predilection for the thigh is not a restriction to a proper subset.
source_name: Cancers (2020) Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma: State of the Art

rationale: Synonym of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma; occurs in deep soft tissue at multiple sites across the connective/soft-tissue ceiling, so not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Cancers (2020) Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma: State of the Art

rationale: Mesenchymal chondrosarcoma has a widespread distribution involving both bone (craniofacial, ribs/chest wall, spine, extremities) and extraskeletal soft tissue (~30-40% of cases), covering both compartments of its bone-plus-soft-tissue ceiling.
source_name: Skeletal Radiology (2020) Mesenchymal chondrosarcoma: imaging and clinical findings

rationale: Clear cell chondrosarcoma has a predilection for the epiphyses of long bones (proximal femur/humerus) but also arises in flat bones, spine, ribs, hands/feet and skull; a predilection within the skeleton is not a restriction to a proper subset of its bone-only ceiling.
source_name: Diagnostic Cytopathology (2020) Clear-cell chondrosarcomas

rationale: Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma arises across the chondrosarcoma spectrum, chiefly in skeletal sites (pelvis, femur, humerus) but also reported in sinonasal/craniofacial sites; evidence does not cleanly restrict it to a proper subset of its ceiling.
source_name: Cancers (2023) Classification of Chondrosarcoma

rationale: Giant cell tumor/sarcoma of bone is a skeletal neoplasm (long bones, flat bones, spine, pelvis, and rarely skull/facial bones); it does not arise from the nasal cavity (C300) or paranasal sinus (C31) mucosal sites also present in this code's ceiling, so it is restricted to the bone codes.
source_name: RadioGraphics (2013) Giant Cell Tumor of Bone: Review

term: Giant cell tumor of bone, dedifferentiated
rationale: A bone-based giant cell tumor variant; occurs in the skeleton (predominantly long bones, also axial and craniofacial bones) and not in the nasal cavity/sinus mucosal sites in the ceiling, restricting it to the bone codes.
source_name: RadioGraphics (2013) Giant Cell Tumor of Bone: Review

term: Giant cell tumor of bone, malignant
rationale: Malignant giant cell tumor of bone is a skeletal neoplasm arising in long bones, flat/axial bones and rarely craniofacial bones; it does not arise in the nasal cavity or paranasal sinus mucosa in the ceiling, so it is restricted to the bone codes.
source_name: RadioGraphics (2013) Giant Cell Tumor of Bone: Review

rationale: Osteoclastoma is a synonym for giant cell tumor of bone, a skeletal tumor; it does not arise from nasal cavity/paranasal sinus mucosa in the ceiling, restricting it to the bone codes.
source_name: RadioGraphics (2013) Giant Cell Tumor of Bone: Review

term: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath, malignant
rationale: Malignant tenosynovial giant cell tumor arises from synovium/tendon sheaths in soft tissue across multiple limb and other connective-tissue sites, spanning its soft-tissue-only ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9252/3 Malignant tenosynovial giant cell tumor, C49._)

rationale: This tumor arises from synovial/tendon-sheath soft tissue at multiple anatomic sites (hands, feet, large joints and other soft tissues), covering the connective/soft-tissue ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9252/3, C49._)

rationale: Adamantinoma of long bones occurs in ~97% of cases in the long tubular limb bones (chiefly tibia, also fibula/humerus/radius/femur); it is restricted to limb bones (C40) and effectively excludes the axial/craniofacial bones (C41) present in the ceiling.
source_name: In Vivo (2021) Adamantinoma: An Updated Review

rationale: By definition a tumor of the long (limb) bones; ~97% arise in long tubular bones, predominantly the tibia, restricting it to limb-bone codes (C40) rather than the axial/craniofacial bones (C41) in the ceiling.
source_name: In Vivo (2021) Adamantinoma: An Updated Review

rationale: Classic adamantinoma is a biphasic neoplasm of long bones that predominantly involves the tibia (and occasionally fibula), restricting it to the limb-bone codes (C40) and not the axial/craniofacial bones (C41) in the ceiling.
source_name: Clinical Tree - Adamantinoma of Long Bone (Dorfman/Czerniak)

rationale: Classic adamantinoma is a long-bone tumor predominantly of the tibia/fibula, restricting it to limb-bone codes (C40) rather than the axial and craniofacial bones (C41) present in the ceiling.
source_name: Clinical Tree - Adamantinoma of Long Bone

rationale: A variant of long-bone adamantinoma, which arises almost exclusively in the long (limb) bones, chiefly the tibia; restricted to the limb-bone codes (C40) rather than axial/craniofacial bones (C41) in the ceiling.
source_name: In Vivo (2021) Adamantinoma: An Updated Review

rationale: Tibial adamantinoma by name and clinical reality arises in the tibia (the long bones of the lower limb, C402), which is the overwhelmingly dominant site (80-85% of adamantinomas); this is a strict single-site subset of the code's bone ceiling.
source_name: In Vivo (2021) Adamantinoma: An Updated Review

rationale: An odontogenic sarcoma of the tooth-bearing jaws; its ceiling is already limited to the jaw bones (C410 bones of skull/face incl. maxilla, C411 mandible) and the entity occurs in both jaws, so it is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9290/3 odontogenic)

rationale: An odontogenic jaw sarcoma; ceiling already restricted to jaw bones (C410, C411) and the tumor occurs in both maxilla and mandible, so not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9290/3)

rationale: An odontogenic jaw sarcoma occurring in both the maxilla and mandible; ceiling already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411), so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9290/3)

rationale: Under 9310/3 this is the jaw (odontogenic) ameloblastoma/adamantinoma; its ceiling is only the jaw-bone codes (C410 skull/face incl. maxilla, C411 mandible) and it occurs in both, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9310/3 Ameloblastoma, malignant)

rationale: Malignant ameloblastoma of the jaws arises in both the mandible (majority) and maxilla; the ceiling is already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411), so it is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9310/3)

rationale: Metastasizing ameloblastoma originates in the jaws (mandible more than maxilla); the ceiling is already limited to jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) and both are involved, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9310/3)

rationale: Synonym for metastasizing ameloblastoma of the jaws; occurs in both mandible and maxilla, and the ceiling is already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411), so not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9310/3)

rationale: Odontogenic sarcoma of the jaws; ceiling already limited to jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) with occurrence in both, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3 odontogenic)

rationale: Odontogenic jaw sarcoma; ceiling already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) and the entity occurs in both jaws, so not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

rationale: Ameloblastic fibrosarcoma is an odontogenic sarcoma of the jaws arising in both mandible and maxilla; ceiling already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411), so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

rationale: Synonym for odontogenic (ameloblastic) sarcoma of the jaws; ceiling limited to jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) and occurs in both jaws, so not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

rationale: Odontogenic sarcoma of the tooth-bearing jaws; ceiling already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) with involvement of both, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

rationale: Odontogenic sarcoma NOS arises in the jaws; ceiling limited to jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) and both jaws are involved, so it is not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

rationale: Plural synonym for odontogenic sarcoma of the jaws; ceiling already limited to the two jaw-bone codes (C410, C411) with both jaws involved, so no proper-subset restriction applies.
source_name: ICD-O-3 morphology list (9330/3)

term: Round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions
rationale: This family of undifferentiated round cell sarcomas arises across bone, soft tissue and the central nervous system depending on fusion partner, spanning the multiple compartments in its broad ceiling; a generic multi-site sarcoma descriptor, not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Surgical Pathology Clinics (2025) Sarcomas with EWSR1::non-ETS fusion

rationale: EWSR1/FUS::NFATC2 sarcoma predominates in the long bones but is also reported in soft tissue (extremities, retroperitoneum, chest wall, head and neck), covering both bone and soft-tissue compartments of the ceiling; a predilection for long bones is not a clean proper-subset restriction.
source_name: Surgical Pathology Clinics (2025) Sarcomas with EWSR1::non-ETS fusion

rationale: EWSR1::PATZ1 sarcoma arises in deep soft tissue (chest/abdominal wall, extremities), head and neck, and the central nervous system; it is a multi-compartment (soft tissue plus CNS) entity rather than being restricted to a single clean proper subset of the broad ceiling.
source_name: Surgical Pathology Clinics (2025) Sarcomas with EWSR1::non-ETS fusion

term: Round cell sarcoma with EWSR1::non-ETS fusions
rationale: Synonym for the EWSR1-non-ETS round cell sarcoma family, which occurs across bone, soft tissue and CNS depending on fusion partner; a generic multi-site descriptor, not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Surgical Pathology Clinics (2025) Sarcomas with EWSR1::non-ETS fusion

rationale: CIC-rearranged sarcoma predominates in deep soft tissue (~85%) but also occurs in viscera (~10%), bone (<5%) and the central nervous system, spanning multiple compartments of its broad ceiling; a soft-tissue predilection is not a proper-subset restriction.
source_name: Cancers (2022) CIC-Rearranged Sarcomas

rationale: CIC::DUX4 is the canonical CIC fusion; these sarcomas arise predominantly in soft tissue but are also documented in bone and the central nervous system, covering multiple compartments of the ceiling rather than a single proper subset.
source_name: Cancers (2022) CIC-Rearranged Sarcomas

rationale: Reports suggest CIC::NUTM1 has a distinct tropism for the axial skeleton and, in the CNS literature, is the most common CIC fusion partner in intracranial tumors; the site data are conflicting and based on very few cases, so a proper-subset restriction cannot be established with confidence.
source_name: Cancers (2022) CIC-Rearranged Sarcomas

term: CNS Ewing family tumor with CIC alteration
rationale: This term denotes CIC-rearranged sarcoma arising primarily in the central nervous system, a distinct entity recognized in the 2021 WHO Classification of CNS Tumors; it is by definition restricted to the CNS/meninges/nerve codes within this code's broad bone/soft-tissue/CNS ceiling.
source_name: Brain Pathology (2024) CIC/ATXN1-rearranged tumors in the CNS; WHO CNS 5th ed
